goals.item: Improve prompt quality while controlling context growth and cost
Enforce stronger write safety and idempotency for economic actions
Formalize engine contracts and contract tests
Raise production readiness for telemetry, alerts, and diagnostics

non_goals.item: Replacing Neo4j with alternate graph storage in v1.4
Redesigning existing API namespace or removing /v1 compatibility
Director engine machine-readable contract — Director remains rules-based with no contract validation in v1.4; contract deferred to post-v1.4

strengths.item: Your plan keeps graph authority explicit and avoids hidden engine state coupling.
You correctly separate context selection from context compression.
You prioritize deterministic logic (relevance/gossip/rules) for replayable debugging.
You define practical first deliverables in an order that unlocks downstream work.

finding.issue: Proposed file layout diverges from current repository structure.
finding.reasoning: The repository uses api/routes and domain subfolders under engines; introducing parallel api/routers and engines/*.py will create duplication and coupling.
finding.fix: Keep existing structure; add new modules under current directories only (for example engines/dialogue, engines/economy, retrieval, graph, api/routes).

finding.issue: Idempotency is required but deduplication storage and TTL are unspecified.
finding.reasoning: Without explicit persistence and conflict semantics, retries can still double-apply currency or quest rewards.
finding.fix: Introduce IdempotencyRecord storage with Neo4j as canonical source of truth and Redis as cache-only accelerator, including key scope, payload hash, status, response hash, created_at, expires_at.

finding.issue: Currency atomicity boundary is underspecified for item plus currency transfers.
finding.reasoning: Trading operations can drift if item transfer and balance transfer are not in one transaction.
finding.fix: Route buy and sell through a single graph_writer transaction coordinator that updates ownership, balances, and audit edges atomically.

finding.issue: Compression cache invalidation is defined conceptually but not canonically sourced.
finding.reasoning: Missing invalidation authority leads to stale context and nondeterministic prompt content.
finding.fix: Make last_graph_updated_at the sole invalidation signal; derive cache key from node_id, node_type, prompt_schema_version, compression_prompt_version.

finding.issue: Engine contracts are proposed but no enforcement path is defined.
finding.reasoning: YAML contracts without test verification become stale documentation.
finding.fix: Add contract_tests that load contracts and assert required events, side effects, idempotency behavior, and auth scope.

finding.issue: Event provenance schema is good but migration strategy is missing.
finding.reasoning: Existing events from v1.3 may not carry producer/schema_version/origin_engine.
finding.fix: Add migration script to backfill provenance with defaults and mark inferred=true where needed.

finding.issue: Metrics cardinality risk is not constrained.
finding.reasoning: Labels including npc_id/request_id can explode time-series volume.
finding.fix: Restrict labels to bounded dimensions (engine, route, result, tier) and log high-cardinality values only in JSON logs.

finding.issue: LLM fallback behaviors are implied but not explicit per boundary.
finding.reasoning: v1 coding rules require boundary fallback contracts for LLM and graph failures.
finding.fix: Define fallback matrix per endpoint and engine: LLM timeout fallback response, graph unavailable 503, validation failure 422 with structured details.

finding.issue: Awareness cache TTL is fixed in prose.
finding.reasoning: Hardcoded values conflict with no-magic-values principles.
finding.fix: Move awareness TTL and cache namespace to config.py and llm_config.yaml.

finding.issue: Director and Economy are optional but rollout gating is not explicit.
finding.reasoning: Optional systems can leak side effects if partially enabled.
finding.fix: Gate with explicit feature flags and contract-level disabled behavior tests.

principles.item: Graph is authoritative for game state and relationships.
Only graph_writer (and sub-writers called by it) performs Cypher writes.
Existing direct write paths are migrated incrementally to graph_writer-coordinated flows during v1.4.
Engines consume graph data plus explicit contracts; engines never read private state from other engines.
Every mutating flow emits typed Event nodes with provenance metadata.
All external boundaries validate first and fail fast.

clients.item: Unity and Unreal via REST and WebSocket under /v1/*

api_layer.item: FastAPI routes in api/routes with composition root in api/dependencies.py

engine_layer.item: Dialogue, Gossip, Event, Quest, Trading, Faction, Reputation, Awareness, Director
New: Context Relevance Engine and Currency Verification Engine

core_layer.item: Neo4j graph and graph services under graph/
LLM adapters behind LLMClientProtocol under engines/llm/
Schema loaders and validators under schema/
Neo4j as source of truth for durable state and idempotency records
Redis optional for non-idempotency caches such as short-lived context and awareness data

module.reason: Deterministic item ranking before budget enforcement
Economy namespace aligned with existing domain layout
Safe and auditable currency mutation boundary
Tier budget policy and compression trigger logic
Loads versioned compression templates from docs prompt source
Versioned prompt templates (including compression templates) per prompt hygiene rules
Parameterized balance and audit edge writes
End-to-end simulation of graph creation and multi-turn gameplay flows
Single source of truth for token budgets, compression rules, and currency limits
Asyncio background task that hard-deletes expired idempotency records every IDEMPOTENCY_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS

common_invariants.item: All new v1.4 mutating endpoints require X-Idempotency-Key header and meta {actor, reason, request_id} body object. This includes the dialogue endpoint.
Legacy v1.3 mutating endpoints moved under v1.4 rollout must fail fast when X-Idempotency-Key is missing, with clear error code and message.
Mutating flows emit Event with producer, origin_engine, schema_version, and provenance.
Soft delete default path for gameplay operations; hard delete restricted to admin scope only.
Unknown game_action values are logged as warnings and ignored for mutation, while dialogue response text is preserved.
No currency field can change except through Currency Verification Engine paths.

transport.item: Header-based transport in v1.4: clients must send X-Idempotency-Key for mutating endpoints.
Request body idempotency_key is not accepted to avoid dual-source ambiguity.

key_format.item: Idempotency key format is UUIDv4 string only in v1.4.
Non-UUIDv4 keys are rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID.

storage.item: Neo4j is canonical source of truth for idempotency record state.
v1.4 idempotency decisions are served from Neo4j only.

record_fields.item: pending_timeout_seconds: int (default 30) — used to detect crashed in-flight requests

retention_policy.item: Retention window is fixed to 24 hours in v1.4.
expires_at must equal created_at plus 24 hours.
Replay requests after expiration are treated as new requests.
Expired records are hard-deleted by a scheduled asyncio background task running every IDEMPOTENCY_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 3600); it deletes records WHERE expires_at < datetime().

behavior.item: Missing idempotency key returns HTTP 400 with stable error code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.
Empty or malformed idempotency key returns HTTP 422 with stable error code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID.
Same key plus same request_hash returns previous result (safe replay).
Same key plus different request_hash returns HTTP 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT.
Replay of a pending record within pending_timeout_seconds returns HTTP 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT; client should retry after the timeout window.
Replay of a pending record whose created_at is older than pending_timeout_seconds is treated as a crashed request: re-execute and overwrite the record in place.
Idempotency lookup and replay decisions do not depend on Redis availability.

example.condition: X-Idempotency-Key header is missing on mutating endpoint.
X-Idempotency-Key is present but not valid UUIDv4.
example.response_shape: {"success": false, "error": "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID", "message": "X-Idempotency-Key must be a valid UUIDv4.", "request_id": "..."}

example.condition: Same idempotency key reused with different request_hash within retention window.
example.response_shape: {"success": false, "error": "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT", "message": "Idempotency key already used for a different request.", "request_id": "..."}

example.condition: Replay of a key whose record is pending and created_at is within pending_timeout_seconds.
example.response_shape: {"success": false, "error": "IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT", "message": "Request is still being processed. Retry after pending_timeout_seconds.", "request_id": "..."}

inputs.item: X-Idempotency-Key (header, required — same rules as all v1.4 mutating endpoints)

flow.item: Validate X-Idempotency-Key header; check idempotency record; replay cached response if same key and request_hash found (no re-mutation).
Gather candidate context from graph and retrieval sources.
Run context relevance scoring and top-K selection per tier.
Run budget enforcement and conditional compression.
Build deterministic prompt and call structured LLM response path.
Validate response via Pydantic schema before any mutation.
Apply bounded relation deltas and route currency-bearing actions to currency engine.

rules.item: Dialogue requires X-Idempotency-Key header; missing key returns 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.
Tier A is never compressed; if Tier A exceeds budget, raise ContextBudgetError.
Relation delta bounds enforce per-turn and sliding-window safety.

inputs.item: candidate_context_items with {id, type, recency, severity, proximity, relation_relevance, quest_involvement, explicit_flag}

tier_policy.item: Context tiers are fixed in v1.4: Tier 0, Tier A, Tier B, Tier C.
session_turns are a named sub-tier of Tier A with their own configurable token sub-budget (session_turns_budget_tokens in llm_config.yaml); session_turns are never compressed.
Tier model may be generalized in a later release without changing v1.4 contracts.

scoring.formula: score = w_recency*norm_recency + w_severity*norm_severity + w_proximity*norm_proximity + w_relation*norm_relation + w_quest*norm_quest + w_explicit*explicit_flag
scoring.proximity_definition: Minimum graph hops between the NPC and the context item's referenced characters or locations. 0 hops = same node; scores decay linearly to 0 at max_proximity_hops (config default 2); items beyond max_proximity_hops receive proximity score of 0.
scoring.tie_breaking: Equal-score items are sorted by (node_type ASC, id ASC) to guarantee deterministic prompt assembly per rule PROMPT-05.

behavior.item: Tokenize each tier with backend-appropriate tokenizer.
If tier token usage exceeds compression_trigger_ratio of the tier budget, compress in order Tier B then Tier C.

Cache compressed outputs keyed by (node_id, node_type, prompt_schema_version, compression_prompt_version) only; last_graph_updated_at is stored alongside the cached value and used as the sole invalidation signal — content_hash is not part of the cache key.
Invalidate cache entry when stored last_graph_updated_at differs from current node value.

fallbacks.item: Compression failure does not bypass budget checks; raises typed error with tier diagnostics.

rules.item: Prerequisites validated through graph_reader before offer.
Item rewards route through trading engine; currency rewards route through currency engine.
Quest failed_reason carries a visibility flag (player | admin); default is admin to avoid leaking hidden game mechanics; game designers set visibility per failure type in the quest definition.
Emit Event for each lifecycle transition.

currency_rules.item: Currency amounts are integer smallest units only; decimal currency is not allowed in v1.4.
Currency transfer and reward amount must be strictly positive integers greater than zero.
Amounts above configured upper bound fail with deterministic validation error.
Validate sufficient funds and configured per-transaction max.
Validate cumulative per-session max to prevent LLM abuse.

Insufficient-funds check and balance debit are atomic: currency_writer uses WHERE c.currency_balance >= $amount inside the Neo4j ACID transaction so no separate pre-read is needed and concurrent transfers cannot both succeed against the same balance.
Persist TRANSFERRED_TO audit edge with amount, reason, request_id.
Dialogue cannot mint currency directly; only validated action path can mutate balances.

faction_engine.item: Writer-oriented engine for MEMBER_OF and FACTION_RELATION updates.
Emits events for faction standing transitions.

reputation_engine.item: Cache invalidated when contributors hash changes.

awareness_engine.item: Returns active NPC presence snapshot per location.
Cache in Redis with configurable TTL and invalidation on movement.

director_engine.item: Runs on slow scheduler tick and emits events or quest triggers.

migration_requirements.item: Backfill missing event provenance fields for pre-v1.4 events.
Initialize currency_balance for existing characters and shops.
Preserve idempotency with migration-safe default values.

versioning_policy.item: Contract version is tied to release version (for example v1.4.x) and is not dynamically computed at runtime.

enforcement.item: CI must fail if contract YAML changed without corresponding engine_contract_tests updates.

make check-contracts CI target validates that each contract YAML under engines/contracts/ has a corresponding test module in tests/engine_contract_tests/; fails with a diff if any YAML exists without a matching test file.
Contract tests validate emitted event names and minimum payload schema.
Engine contract tests run on every PR for small deterministic scenarios.

compliance_scope.item: Strictly enforced for all new files and all files modified in v1.4 phases.
Legacy files not touched in v1.4 remain tracked as technical debt and are refactored incrementally.

coding_principles_compliance.rule: Module additions are single-purpose and follow existing package boundaries.
New LLM and vector behavior remains behind protocol and factory extension points.
Dependencies are injected via constructors and api/dependencies composition root.
Token limits, cache TTLs, and economic bounds are config-driven (no magic constants).
Context and mutation payloads are immutable copies, not in-place mutation.
Type hints required on all new public methods.
Cross-layer payloads use Pydantic models only.
Boundary validation for API, LLM output, graph reads, and config files.
Writers receive transaction/session injection; they do not open sessions.
Budget enforcement before LLM invocation is mandatory.
All Cypher remains parameterized; no string interpolation for user inputs.

boundary.name: LLM structured generation
boundary.on_error: Return typed fallback dialogue and zero side-effect actions; log llm_validation_failures_total increment.

boundary.name: LLM timeout
boundary.on_error: Serve fallback_responses content and return success response with degraded=true metadata.

boundary.name: Graph unavailable
boundary.on_error: Raise GraphUnavailableError and return HTTP 503 with request_id correlation.

boundary.name: Request validation failure
boundary.on_error: Return HTTP 422 with structured validation details and accepted values where applicable.

boundary.name: Awareness cache (Redis) unavailable
boundary.on_error: Fall back to direct Neo4j query for awareness snapshot; log cache_miss_fallback=true and increment awareness_cache_miss_total metric; do not raise 503.

security.item: Scope model retained: graph_admin is strict superset of graph_write.

operations.item: Feature flags for Director, Economy, Trading, and contract-enforcement strict mode are enabled by default.
Environment defaults: dev=enabled, staging=enabled, prod=enabled with kill-switch support.

Feature flag kill-switches are environment variable overrides that take precedence over config file settings: FEATURE_ECONOMY_ENABLED, FEATURE_TRADING_ENABLED, FEATURE_DIRECTOR_ENABLED (set to false to disable at runtime without a deploy).
Disabled-mode behavior must be deterministic and covered by contract tests for each feature flag.
Admin reindex endpoint retained for manual recovery workflows.
Deployment profile keeps Neo4j community + Redis suitable for POC scale.
Redis degraded mode must be supported for non-idempotency caches only; idempotency behavior remains unchanged when Redis is unavailable.

tradeoffs.item: Richer prompts improve roleplay quality but increase token cost; relevance-first plus selective compression keeps costs bounded.
Numeric currency fields keep schema simple; dedicated currency engine enforces economic safety and auditability.
Deterministic heuristics improve reproducibility and debug quality, while LLM remains focused on narrative generation.
